comparison: Both evaluate claims C29-C31 regarding Rfree improvements and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes consistency with theoretical expectations and lack of overfitting. Peer reviewers accept the findings but note the improvement magnitude is modest and question whether maintained Rfree is a strong argument in favor of the model.

Both evaluate claims C32-C34 regarding increased multiconformer residues and find them SUPPORTED. Both agree qFit successfully detects conformational heterogeneity. Peer reviewers specifically note the algorithm 'does not introduce spurious or unnecessary conformational heterogeneity.'

Both evaluate claims C37-C40 regarding geometry improvements and find them SUPPORTED. Both agree multiconformer modeling improves geometry metrics. Peer reviewers add a caveat that 'total absence of geometric outliers is not necessarily required' at high resolution where data should have freedom to place atoms.

Both evaluate claims C21-C27 describing qFit's core algorithm and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes clear documentation and methodological contributions. Peer reviewers accept the algorithmic description as 'well designed' but note lack of detail on BIC performance metrics and how sharply it identifies best models.

Both evaluate claims C58-C61 regarding test dataset composition. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED with appropriate criteria. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning exclusion of ligands and multichain models, which 'may convey the impression that qFit cannot handle such use cases.'

Both evaluate resolution-dependent performance claims. OpenEval evaluates C41-C44 as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate guidance on method applicability. Peer reviewers evaluate overlapping claims C41-C44, C48 as SUPPORTED, accepting the validation approach and characterization of resolution limitations.

Both evaluate claims C52, C69-C70 regarding cryo-EM challenges and find them SUPPORTED. Both agree these represent significant issues in the field. Peer reviewers note the manuscript 'clearly explains the hurdles' including lack of uniformity in reporting and differences in map treatment.

Both evaluate claims C73-C75 regarding qFit's limitations with poor input models and find them SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes importance for understanding appropriate use cases. Peer reviewers accept these limitations and note the manuscript 'serves as a very useful guide for users in evaluating if and when qFit should be applied.'

Both evaluate claims C35-C36 regarding rotamer consistency. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED based on Figure 2D analysis. Peer reviewers also find them SUPPORTED (grouped with C71-C72), noting 'careful and extensive analysis' and treating examples as convincing demonstrations.

Both evaluate claims C71-C72 regarding new rotamer identification. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED but notes coupled motion inference is speculative. Peer reviewers find them SUPPORTED (grouped with C35-C36), accepting them as evidence of qFit's performance capabilities.

Both evaluate computational improvements claims C62, C66-C68. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED as methodological details with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting the paper 'does not provide...quantitation of the effects of these specific improvements, such as...whether the code faster.'

Both evaluate qFit method description claims. OpenEval evaluates C5-C7, C16-C20 as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers evaluate overlapping claims C5-C6, C17-C18, C47 as UNCERTAIN, acknowledging qFit as 'state-of-the-art' but noting lack of comparison to previous iterations and quantitation of specific improvements.

Both evaluate limitation claims C49-C50. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED by resolution dependence data and poor performance on high Rfree structures. Peer reviewers evaluate these (grouped with C73-C75) as SUPPORTED, accepting the limitations and recommendations as well-documented practical constraints.

Both evaluate cryo-EM application claims C45-C46. OpenEval finds them SUPPORTED, noting ability to recapitulate manual models and identify new conformations. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, finding the section 'enlightening' but noting 'analysis of its performance is more limited due to a limited number of high-resolution test cases.'

Both address claim C55 regarding file format compatibility. OpenEval evaluates C53-C55 as SUPPORTED, reflecting knowledge of format standards. Peer reviewers rate C7, C55 as UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification on 'how/whether qFit models can be further refined afterwards' in other software.

OpenEval evaluates summary claims C47-C48 as SUPPORTED by collective manuscript data. Peer reviewers evaluate C47 (grouped with method claims) as UNCERTAIN, questioning lack of comparison to previous qFit versions despite acknowledging 'convincing examples.'

OpenEval evaluates summary claim C48 as SUPPORTED by collective data. Peer reviewers evaluate C48 (grouped with resolution claims C41-C44) as SUPPORTED, accepting the resolution-dependent performance characterization.

OpenEval evaluates background claims C1-C3, C8-C11 as SUPPORTED, establishing biological and methodological context through established knowledge and citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these foundational claims.

OpenEval evaluates background claims C4, C12-C15 as SUPPORTED, describing challenges of manual modeling and advantages of multiconformer representations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.

OpenEval evaluates future direction claims C56-C57 as UNCERTAIN, noting C57 is explicitly speculative about potential improvements without supporting data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
